messages.subject: Aggregating a SpatialPolygonsDataFrame
parts:
Hey All,

This should be straightforward; maybe I'm overthinking it, but I'm stuck.

I've got the GADM world polygons, which has admin 2-level polygons, loaded in R as a SpatialPolygonsDataFrame, and I want to aggregate them up to country-wide polygons, and then save the ones belonging to sub-Saharan Africa as a shapefile for later use.

I use unionSpatialPolygons to aggregate the polygons by ISO code, no problem there. But that creates a SpatialPolygons object, not a SpatialPolygonsDataFrame, so I can't save it as a shapefile. I don't actually need any of the data from the original ssa_shp data slot except ISO and perhaps NAME - I'm just going to rasterize it later.

There should be some way to aggregate the data and use SpatialPolygonsDataFrame() to merge them, but I keep getting errors like "row.names of data and Polygons IDs do not match".

--- code ---

library(raster)
library(maptools)

#http://biogeo.ucdavis.edu/data/gadm2/gadm_v2_shp.zip
world <- shapefile('./data/gadm/world/gadm2.shp')

ssa <- c("AGO", "BEN", "BWA", "BFA", "BDI", "CMR", "CPV", "CAF", "TCD", "COM", "COD", "COG", "CIV", "DJI", "GNQ", "ERI", "ETH", "GAB", "GMB", "GHA", "GIN", "GNB", "KEN", "LSO", "LBR", "MDG", "MWI", "MLI", "MRT", "MUS", "MYT", "MOZ", "NAM", "NER", "NGA", "REU", "RWA", "STP", "SEN", "SYC", "SLE", "SOM", "ZAF", "SSD", "SHN", "SDN", "SWZ", "TZA", "TGO", "UGA", "ESH", "ZMB", "ZWE")

i <- which(world$ISO %in% ssa)

ssa_shp <- world[i,]
ssa_shp2 <- unionSpatialPolygons(ssa_shp, ssa_shp$ISO)

##then what?

messages.author: 77ad22fce6691f60
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Aggregating a SpatialPolygonsDataFrame
parts:
Hi Erica, 
I've had this problem before. You just need to create a new SpatialPolygonsDataFrame, providing a new attribute table (data.frame) with row.names that match up to the IDs of the new polygons. This is often just a sequence of numbers starting from 0, but can be text labels too.

newdata <- data.frame(whatever you want in here)
row.names(newdata) <- (however the new polygons are labeled)
ssa_shp2 <- SpatialPolygonsDataFrame(ssa_shp2, data=newdata)

Hope this helps,
Kristy
